findings.description: Regular expression with nested quantifiers vulnerable to ReDoS attack in charset extraction
findings.reasoning: The regex pattern contains nested quantifiers: `.*?` followed by literal text, then `[\"\\']*` followed by `.+?`. This creates potential for catastrophic backtracking when the pattern fails to match, especially with malformed HTML input. The pattern is applied to user-controlled HTML content via findall(), making it exploitable.

evidence.code_context:
charset_re = re.compile(r'<meta.*?charset=["\']*(.+?)["\'>]', flags=re.I)
pragma_re = re.compile(r'<meta.*?content=["\']*;?charset=(.+?)["\'>]', flags=re.I)
xml_re = re.compile(r'^<\?xml.*?encoding=["\']*(.+?)["\'>]')

return (
    charset_re.findall(content)
    + pragma_re.findall(content)
    + xml_re.findall(content)
)
evidence.dataflow_analysis: The regex is compiled with user-controlled HTML content passed to findall(). The pattern has nested quantifiers that can cause exponential backtracking on malformed input.
evidence.notes: This is in the get_encodings_from_content() function which processes HTML content. The nested quantifiers `.*?` and `.+?` combined with character classes create backtracking opportunities.
